question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Slack off
solution:
The correct meaning of the idiom "slack off" is option 2) To ease pressure on something.

**Explanation:**

"Slack off" is an idiom that means to decrease or reduce one's effort or activity, to relax, or to take it easy. It is often used in the context of work or study, where someone who was previously working hard or putting in a lot of effort suddenly starts to work less or become lazy. When someone "slacks off," they are reducing the amount of pressure or workload they are experiencing.

Here are the meanings of the other options in English and Hindi:

To understand a hidden meaning - This option is not the correct meaning of the idiom "slack off." "To understand a hidden meaning" means to discover or comprehend a meaning that is not immediately obvious. In Hindi - एक छिपी हुई अर्थ को समझना

To ease pressure on something - This is the correct meaning of the idiom "slack off." "To ease pressure on something" means to reduce the workload or pressure on something. In Hindi - कुछ पर दबाव कम करना

To make most effort - This option is not the correct meaning of the idiom "slack off." "To make most effort" means to put in the maximum amount of effort possible. In Hindi - सबसे अधिक प्रयास करना

To be very rude - This option is not the correct meaning of the idiom "slack off." "To be very rude" means to be impolite or disrespectful to someone. In Hindi - बहुत अकड़ दिखाना

So, the correct answer to the given question is option 2) To ease pressure on something.
